title: Listed Investment Trusts Trading Policy

tiers.name: EQT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, key management personnel, and all employees of EQTHL and/or any of its wholly or majority owned companies including the Responsible Entity (Equity Trustees Limited), and contractors and consultants who may come into possession of Inside Information.

tiers.name: LIT Partners
tiers.description: Those engaged or contracted with the Responsible Entity in managing and/or administering a LIT, such as DigiCo's external manager. Trades under the LIT Partner's own trading policy, procedures and controls agreed with the Responsible Entity, which must meet the minimum blackout and disclosure standards of this Policy.

tiers.name: LIT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, contractors and consultants of a LIT Partner (e.g. of DigiCo's manager) or any other related account as defined by the LIT Partner's trading policy. This is the tier a DigiCo director or executive falls into.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A spouse, partner or child of an EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner individual, or any other person whom they may be expected to control or have significant influence over, including other immediate family members, business partners, companies or other entities or trusts.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Responsible Entity may specify 'any other period' as an additional Black-out Period; the Policy does not state whether such additional periods are announced or kept confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule and 'Units' is defined narrowly (unit, option over an unissued unit, or right to subscribe), not OTC derivatives generally. An OTC put/call operates to limit the economic risk of holding Units and so falls within the hedging restriction, requiring prior clearance under the Trading Request Procedure.
rules.evidence: may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure

rules.detail: Hedging is named expressly and permitted with prior written clearance; the Policy does not distinguish vested/unvested Units (it is a unit trust holding policy, not an equity incentive scheme).
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved

rules.detail: No mention of a prepaid forward sale, collar monetisation or similar structure; 'Trade' covers buying, selling or transferring an economic interest in Units, which is a stretch to reach a monetisation contract that leaves legal title in place.
Short selling is not named and 'Trade' (buy, sell or transfer economic interest) does not obviously extend to a sale of Units not held.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named. If used to limit economic risk of a Unit holding a CFD is caught as a hedging arrangement requiring clearance; if used speculatively it would instead fall within the short-term/speculative trading restriction, also requiring clearance.
rules.evidence: may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly named and permitted with prior written clearance; no minimum shareholding floor or price-trigger guidance is given.
rules.evidence: may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Granting 'any form of security' over Units (charge, lien, pledge to a bank) is expressly covered by the same clause as margin lending and is permitted with prior clearance.
rules.evidence: may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved

rules.detail: Secured financing over Units of any kind, not just margin loans, is expressly permitted subject to prior clearance under the Trading Request Procedure; no exemption authority or floor is stated.
rules.evidence: may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: On-market round-trip trading within three months of acquisition is restricted unless cleared; the restriction is limited to on-market trades, so an OTC collar entry/unwind is arguably outside its literal scope though still caught as a hedging or secured financing arrangement under 6.ii/6.iii.
rules.evidence: may not engage in short-term or speculative trading in a LIT's Units, i.e. trading in or out of the Units on market within three (3) months of acquiring them, unless written prior clearance to trade has been approved

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (evidence of the executed trade; directors must additionally give written confirmation of nature, price and quantity within 2 business days for ASX reporting)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified generally; 2 business days for the Responsible Entity's directors
clearance.evidence: A clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused without a reason being given. The decision is final and binding. Any clearance refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential ... A clearance to trade is valid for five (5) business days.

clearance.approver: Unclear: s.6 requires clearance 'in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure', but that defined term (clause 5) is expressed to apply to EQT Persons only, while s.2 instead directs LIT Persons to the LIT Partner's own trading policy/procedures agreed with the Responsible Entity
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary of the Responsible Entity (LIT Partner Transactions register, kept confidential)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 7 days of execution of the transaction, or as otherwise agreed in writing with the Responsible Entity
clearance.evidence: LIT Partners and LIT Persons may trade in a LIT's Units provided ... the trade has been executed in accordance with the LIT Partner's trading policy, procedures and/or controls which have been agreed with the Responsible Entity.

short_term.evidence: trading in or out of the Units on market within three (3) months of acquiring them, unless written prior clearance to trade has been approved

exceptions.approver: Responsible Entity's Chair (or EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair if the trading is by the Responsible Entity's Chair), via the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship, where EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners have pressing financial commitments that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling Units

exceptions.approver: Responsible Entity's Chair (or EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair), via the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements

exceptions.approver: Responsible Entity's Chair (or EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair in the case of proposed trading by the Responsible Entity's Chair)
exceptions.evidence: any other exceptional circumstances as determined by the Responsible Entity's Chair

Those that do not result in a change to the beneficial interest in the Units (such as transferring Units already held personally into a superannuation fund), and where prior written notification has been given to the Company Secretary
an acquisition of Units under the LIT's distribution reinvestment plan, excluding an election to vary participation

external_documents: The LIT Partner's own trading policy, procedures and/or controls agreed with the Responsible Entity, which governs the clearance mechanics actually applied to LIT Persons and LIT Partners (e.g. DigiCo's manager and its directors).
exemption_authority: Responsible Entity's Chair determines exceptional-circumstances relief (or the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair where the proposed trading is by the Responsible Entity's Chair), on consultation with the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.topic: clearance route ambiguity for LIT Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted trading (short-term, hedging, margin lending/security) requires clearance 'in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure' for EQT Persons, LIT Persons and LIT Partners alike (s.6), but the defined term 'Trading Request Procedure' is drafted as the clause-5 process EQT Persons must follow, while s.2 instead routes LIT Persons/Partners to the LIT Partner's own agreed trading policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a DigiCo director or executive (a LIT Person under the manager, not an EQT Person of Equity Trustees), the bank cannot be certain from this document alone who actually approves a collar or its secured loan leg; the manager's own trading policy (not in this PDF) needs to be obtained and checked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy governs trading in LIT Units generally; there is no employee equity incentive scheme, unvested holding or holding lock referenced anywhere.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no unvested-collateral prohibition or vesting-based carve-out to negotiate around; the only conditions on a funded collar are the blackout periods, clearance and Inside Information rules that apply to any holding.

bespoke_clauses.clause: may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban secured financing outright, this Policy makes both the collar derivatives and the loan's security interest a clearable, not prohibited, category, so a funded collar is structurally available subject to clearance and timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no clause addressing a lender's or counterparty's forced sale, margin call liquidation, or price triggers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no drafted consequence if the bank's collateral call or exercise falls inside a Black-out Period; this residual risk should be raised with the Company Secretary when seeking clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in the day to day management of the buy-back are subject to a further Black-out Period from the buy-back decision date to the next full business day after completion.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the Fund is conducting a unit buy-back, collar timing for an informed manager-side individual must clear an additional, narrower blackout window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Connected Person must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure prior to trading in Units.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan structured through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the clearance requirement.

summary: A funded collar is structurally available under this Policy, unlike an outright ban: hedging (s.6.ii) and any arrangement granting security over the Units, including a margin loan (s.6.iii), are both expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance, so both the derivative legs and the bank's security interest are clearable rather than prohibited. The real uncertainty is who grants that clearance for a DigiCo director or executive, since they sit in the 'LIT Persons' tier whose clearance process is meant to run through the manager's own trading policy (not in this document) even though s.6 also cross-refers to the EQT-specific Trading Request Procedure; the manager's own policy should be obtained before proceeding. Any entry, unwind or exercise must fall outside the half-year and full-year NTA/NAV blackout periods, any PDS/general-meeting/buy-back blackout, and while the individual holds no Inside Information. The Policy does not use a vesting concept, sets no minimum shareholding requirement or price-trigger guidance, and is silent on a lender's forced sale during a blackout period, so those risks are unaddressed rather than prohibited. Overall: likely available with prior written clearance (valid 5 business days for EQT Persons; term unspecified for LIT Persons) once the correct approver is confirmed, and best timed for tenor of at least three months to sit outside the short-term trading restriction.
